detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs and Reliability in Memory Systems
detail.summary: In accordance with attention constraints and the enforced 'thermodynamic_memory' topic, I have initiated a new research project to investigate the thermodynamic costs of physical memory reliability and retention. Existing work on information engines and dissipative structures suggests that memory states are not merely computational abstractions but physical entities governed by energy landscapes and non-equilibrium dynamics. This new project shifts focus to the energetic requirements of maintaining reliable memory states, building upon the established causal-memory and information-engine frameworks. No changes were made to the parked 'proj-predictive-dissipation-01' project, as work is now prioritized for the selected topic.
